whisper.text: If you're watching this, I want to say thank you for purchasing the height adjustment mast. This is a quick start guide on how to set up your pre-assembled mast system that should arrive in the mail looking something like this. Might be a little bit different in the prototypes as I change things, but for the most part it looks like this and should come fairly assembled. You'll notice that this bottom race is loose, so it might just be on here and that's okay. It has a bearing on the bottom. But let's get into it. You have your mast. This is the stock VIVOR mast, but this will work also for the Cut Kit version 2 and even the Cut Kit version 1 if you specify in your order. So the first things first, you'll have this bearing and this retaining ring which clamps onto the bottom of the post. So you just slide it around. You can set it into place for now. The next thing is we'll put the rest of the mast on here and you'll notice that the top portion has a little indent for the mast to sit in. And you're going to need your quill at this point so you get it ready in your other hand. You can put your quill on the rod and then stick the forks, as you can see, around the quill. It slides right over it and then slide everything down into place. The top cap, make sure that the rod goes into the bottom bearing here. And then what you can do is you can make sure that the top cap is seated on the mast and tighten everything down with a hex key number five millimeter. A five millimeter hex key, I think a 5-30 seconds also works. So we'll tighten the top and the bottom here. Doesn't need to be too crazy tight, just snug enough so that things don't move around. And this should be fairly adjusted so that the rod is just at the bottom of the bearing. It might stick out just a little bit and that's okay. But if you need to adjust it, I'll take the top off here. Oops. Make sure I don't knock the mast over. You need to be careful while you're doing this. Now that I have this in place, I'll put my quick spin nut on here. If you need these knurled knobs, let me know. I make them as well. You can take this top cap off if you need to adjust things, and there should just be a nut underneath the top here. And you can hold the rod and loosen it and that'll lower the thread. Or you can raise it up if you really want to. And it should be fairly set for the height of your mast. And then put your nut back on, or excuse me, your adjustment wheel on top. And just tighten that down with the 5mm hex key. And at this point, you're pretty much done with the installation. You'll go clockwise to raise the mast, as you can see. Counterclockwise to lower it. And depending on which iteration, I have a knob on top, either a handled version if you want, or an indent version, like a scrub wheel. And then you can just tighten that down with the 5mm hex key. And then you can raise the rod and lower it. And there you go. That's pretty much it. If you have any questions, let me know. I appreciate, again, your support.
